articles.title: Glenn Close cries! John Malkovich weeps! But it’s Nathan Fielder everyone wants to talk to at the honorary Oscars
articles.summary: All of Hollywood’s biggest stars are in attendance for the Governors’ awards, but nobody gets drunk and the biggest draw is an awkward documentarian. Timothée Chalamet was seconds away from getting into trouble.
body: The Governors awards had a curiously school-like atmosphere this year. Even the carpet in the Ray Dolby Ballroom was faded and striped. The social structure was much the same: closed-off and insular, with cliques, alliances, legendary enmities and intricate hierarchies of popularity and influence. There were those who seemed entirely comfortable – Chalamet, Holland, Tom Cruise, Matt Damon, Willem Dafoe, Seth Rogen – and others still angling for a better table.

Two hours earlier, I had arrived in a Toyota hybrid, almost certainly the worst car in the lot, wearing a jacket from Goodwill. At 4pm, the reception was still relatively quiet. There was a bar, a s’mores station and a playlist of default office-party songs: Timbaland, Rihanna, that sort of thing.
points: All of Hollywood’s biggest stars are in attendance for the Governors’ awards, but nobody gets drunk and the biggest draw is an awkward documentarian.
Timothée Chalamet was seconds away from getting into trouble.

articles.title: The man with the golden touch: James Bond franchise is a money-spinner
articles.summary: Big-screen debut of Ian Fleming’s creation in 1962, with Sean Connery as lead in Dr No, was start of marketing dream. New James Bond announced... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson. Share your thoughts on the casting. Peter Bradshaw’s take. Robert Pattinson’s journey to James Bond.
body: James Bond may be 73 years old but the superspy holds a licence to print money, at the centre of an evergreen multibillion-pound franchise spanning blockbuster films, merchandise, licensing deals and sponsorship.
The announcement that the Twilight and Batman actor Robert Pattinson is the next Bond comes seven years after Daniel Craig revealed that No Time To Die would be his last outing as 007.

This means that by the time Pattinson makes his first appearance it will have been the longest gap in instalments in the 64-year history of the film franchise, an agonisingly long hiatus for the centrepiece of a sprawling commercial enterprise.

While Ian Fleming initially struggled to get Hollywood interested in his debonair, womanising British novel creation, the big-screen debut of Sean Connery in 1962’s Dr No marked the start of a marketing dream.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to James Bond: ‘The honour of a lifetime’
articles.summary: The 40-year-old British actor has had a remarkable career and is back again with the coveted 007. New James Bond announced... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson. Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond.
body: There are big years in an actor’s career, and then there is Robert Pattinson ’s 2026.

This year the 40-year-old Briton has been the face of everything from Kristoffer Borgli’s relationship satire The Drama to Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime. Now, in the culmination of a remarkable run, he has landed the most coveted role in British cinema: James Bond.

After weeks of intense speculation, on Monday the official Bond accounts confirmed Pattinson as the seventh actor to play 007. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said.

Pattinson was easily the most famous of the contenders, and an unusual one: an arthouse actor with a franchise heart-throb’s profile. “Is Robert Pattinson the last true movie star?” the New York Times asked in 2024.
points: The 40-year-old British actor has had a remarkable career and is back again with the coveted 007.

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Extended Cut Sets December Release Date in Theaters
articles.summary: The re-release of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which features footage previously left on the cutting room floor, hits theaters on Dec. 4. Tickets go on sale Nov. 19. News that “Brand New Day” was returning to theaters with an extended cut first broke in late September.
body: Dawson’s Night Nurse is a medic who helps treat injured superheroes. The character first appeared in the first season of “Daredevil” in 2015. Dawson reprised the role in several MCU shows, including “Jessica Jones,” “Luke Cage,” “Iron Fist” and “The Defenders.”

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” first arrived in cinemas on July 31 and skyrocketed as the summer’s biggest blockbuster success. The superhero tentpole debuted to $927 million worldwide on opening weekend and has since extended its global tally to $2.5 billion. Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film is currently the third-highest-grossing movie of all time behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion).

In less than two months of release, “Brand New Day” overtook 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” as the highest-grossing domestic film in history. “The Force Awakens” set the bar at $936 million domestic, and the record stood for over a decade. “Brand New Day” snatched the crown after grossing $936.773 million in 47 days in North American cinemas.

articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Filmmakers Grateful for ‘Light Being Shone’ on Their Film Through Awards Conversation but Prioritize Impact: It’s a ‘Small Cog in a Machine of Resistance’
articles.summary: Over the last few years, leading documentary festival IDFA has become a crucial stop on the awards season trail, with major streamers and key studios courting voters in Amsterdam’s imposing 17th-century canalside houses and theaters.
body: The panel saw a rare public appearance by director Yuval Abraham, who connected via Zoom from London, where he continues to tackle his journalism work for “NAZA” producer The Guardian, represented on the IDFA stage by editorial director, film and TV and head of documentaries Lindsay Poulton. Abraham and Poulton were joined by the film’s producer James Wilson (“The Zone of Interest”) and Fionnuala Jamison, managing director of major sales agent MK2. Rachel Szor, who directed the film alongside Abraham, was not present.

Asked about how it feels to tackle the overwhelming calendar of a high-profile awards campaign for a film as sensitive and somber as “NAZA,” Abraham said the thought is not at the forefront of his mind. “We have so much to do with the film and also with the journalism. We’re working on the investigative journalism, and I really want to focus on that.”

articles.summary: The name is Pattinson, Robert Pattinson, but who will be his first Bond Girl? Amazon MGM Studios has made it official, naming the 40-year-old Brit the next James Bond in the exclusive franchise, with Denis Villeneuve helming the next film from a script by Steven Knight and Amy Pascal and David…
body: But 007 is only as good as the women standing next to him, and the franchise has included some memorable (as well as some less memorable) selections over the years. Some of those the classics include Ursula Andress’ Honey Ryder in “Dr. No” (1962), Diana Rigg’s Teresa di Vicenza in “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service” (1969) and Honor Blackman’s Pussy Galore in “Goldfinger” (1964), as well as more recent standouts such as Michelle Yeoh’s Wai Lin in “Tomorrow Never Dies” (1997), Eva Green’s Vesper Lynd in “Casino Royale” (2006) and the most recent, Léa Seydoux, who was Madeleine Swann in both “Spectre” and “No Time To Die” (2021).

The Bond girl (should it evolve to Bond Woman?) is a staple of the franchise. When James Bond was created by author Ian Fleming, many speculated that Fleming’s lover, Muriel Wright, may have been an inspiration for the female characters.

Villeneuve gives us serious reason for optimism, as he has helped shepherd powerful roles for female characters such as Amy Adams in “Arrival,” Emily Blunt in “Sicario” and Rebecca Ferguson and Zendaya in the “Dune” franchise.
Variety lists the best potential Bond girls we’d like to see in the Pattinson iteration.

articles.title: Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch Bring Stand-Up, Sketch and Songs to Hilarious New York Comedy Festival Showcase
articles.summary: Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 brought laughter, cheers and ’90s rock parodies to the New York Comedy Festival on Thursday. The comedians, who represent the funniest and most exciting rising voices in comedy, each performed a seven-minute set for a lively audience at the Venue on Music Row…
body: Variety ’s 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 brought laughter, cheers and ’90s rock parodies to the New York Comedy Festival on Thursday.

Josh Ocean Thomas kicked off the showcase with an energetic punch and jokes about growing up mixed-race and going to Christian school. Adam Friedland brought a lectern on stage and performed a partly improvised bit that involved a lengthy acceptance speech for the award he had not yet been given. And Eilise Patton performed a solo sketch, playing a Goldman Sachs executive preparing to make a difficult phone call.

Shapel Lacey, Wally Baram, Usama Siddiquee and Olivia Carter delivered standout stand-up sets, and Kyle Gordon closed out the show with a full-band performance of his alt-rock satire “If You Break Up With Me” and the ode to nu metal “Crawl to Me,” in which he led the crowd in a NSFW chant: “Suck the dick, drink the piss.”

The comedians accepted their awards on stage and took a class photo with Shanfeld, Hirsch and veteran comedy talent booker Louis Faranda. The performers, attendees and industry folks then headed to the rooftop bar at the Hard Rock for drinks and light bites.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond | Peter Bradshaw
articles.summary: Pattinson is a character actor whose talent for inscrutable appraisal may mean a new era for 007. Will this more willowy, classy Bond leave sexism in the shadows? • New James Bond announced...
body: I f it wasn’t Bond … maybe it would have been Dr No in some hi-tech reboot. But Robert Pattinson – with his movie-star chops and track record in hip A24-type character turns, and his gift for cool, inscrutable appraisal and sensual menace – is an exquisite choice as 007, playing on the darker and more sophisticated notes of Pattinson’s performing personality.

And let’s hope, incidentally, that the actor now isn’t forced into a five-hour daily gym regimen to bulk up. I like the taller and more willowy Bond that Pattinson represents, the Bond from whose frame the tux hangs gracefully, the Bond with elegant abandon who’s a former British Naval officer, not a former US Navy Seal, the Bond who with a crinkly-eyed reptilian grin can style out waking up with a hangover after too many whisky-and-sodas at the baccarat table.
points: Pattinson is a character actor whose talent for inscrutable appraisal may mean a new era for 007.

articles.title: At Least Robert Pattinson Looks the Part…According to Ian Fleming
articles.summary: The Bond author commissioned a sketch of 007 in the 1950s — and it bears an uncanny resemblance to a certain British actor currently being fitted for a tuxedo.
body: Well, it took nearly 70 years, and there were plenty of detours along the way, but Ian Fleming finally got the James Bond of his dreams — at least when it comes to jawline and nose shape.

Connery and Lazenby had dark hair but brown eyes. Craig had blue eyes but fair hair (controversial coloring that inspired more than a few cheeky headlines when he was cast: “No Mr. Blonde, They Expect You To Dye”). Moore had blue eyes but his hair was shades too light. Brosnan came closest, with black hair and blue eyes. But it turns out Fleming had other criteria aside from basic coloring and measurements.

In fact, the author commissioned a portrait of Bond in the 1950s, years before the movies were launched, when a British newspaper purchased the rights to serialize the novels as a cartoon strip. To help the paper’s illustrator nail down the look, Fleming hired an unknown artist to sketch 007’s face according to his highly specific instructions (“I think we should avoid giving Bond an American-shaped head and a duck’s haircut,” he wrote in one note).
points: The Bond author commissioned a sketch of 007 in the 1950s — and it bears an uncanny resemblance to a certain British actor currently being fitted for a tuxedo.
